recipient: East Africa (XEA); recipient organisation not named, recipient unspecified
title: Somaliland E-government Capability Enhancement Project
description: The Ministry of ICT of Somaliland unveiled the Somaliland e-Government Strategy 2020-2024 Action Plan, a government digitalization implementation guideline which requires many external resources for initiation. Government institutions in Somaliland currently work individually with limited information exchange. People have to visit multiple departments to take care of business and the service quality is unsatisfactory. Furthermore, data exchange among government institutions requires lengthy phone calls or communication. This system puts the overall operation under the risk of low efficiency, data mishandling, poor management, and tracking difficulties. As a result, cooperation among government institutions is challenging.This project echoes the 16th and 17th UN Sustainable Development Goals through establishment of channels for the government to be transparent and disperse information to the general public, while also enhancing the government digitization and e-governance capability. The main content of the project is to enhance Somalilands e-government capability through establishing a data exchange platform among government institutions, capacity building and institutional strengthening, and improving government network management.

recipient: SOM; Somali National Bureau of Statistics, named as transaction receiver
title: Somali Integrated Statistics and Economic Planning Capacity Building
description: The objective of the Somali Integrated Statistics and Economic Planning Capacity Building Project for Somalia is to strengthen the national statistical system in the collection, processing and dissemination of poverty and selected macro-economic data to inform development policy and poverty reduction activities. The Project has four components. 1. Strengthening coordination, statistical infrastructure and data development of the national statistical system component will provide support to the client's key official statistics producing agencies in strengthening the capacity of the country's National statistical system (NSS) to collect data for poverty and macroeconomic monitoring. 1.1. Supporting the Development and Coordination of the NSS subcomponent will support the strengthening of the recipient's legal and organizational framework for the NSS as well as statistical infrastructure. 1.2. Somali Integrated Household Budget Survey subcomponent will support the design and implementation of the Somali Integrated Household Budget Survey (SIHBS) for monitoring welfare, providing macroeconomic baselines and establishing a baseline survey for a frequent data collection system. 1.3. Strengthening Sources of Business and Administrative Data needed for the Compilation of National Accounts and Key Social Statistics subcomponent will address key data gaps needed to produce quality national accounts statistics that meet the basics of the System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA2008) and other international statistical standards. 1.4. Strengthening Human Capacity in Poverty, Consumer Price Index (CPI) and National Accounts Statistics subcomponent will support the training of staff to compile poverty indicators and indexes as well as to draw poverty lines, using new data from the poverty survey and new CPI. 1.5. Development of a Compendium of Statistical Concepts and Definitions, Data Access and Information Dissemination Policy subcomponent will support improvement in data management and dissemination practices to strengthen statistical confidentiality and microdata sharing. 2. Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Development and Equipment of the National Statistical System component will provide supports the ICT infrastructure in the DNS and selected key federal level MDAs. It will provide computers, laptops and related IT networking equipment. 2.1. ICT Needs Assessment and ICT Strategy subcomponent will support an ICT needs assessment to identify the hardware/software needed to support the production and dissemination of the social and macroeconomics statistics needed for the compilation of national accounts, CPI and poverty indicators. 2.2. Statistical Software and Hardware subcomponent will finance the acquisition of information technology and communications infrastructure. 3. Data Utilization for Monitoring and Evaluation (M and E) and Planning component has two subcomponents. 3.1. Strengthening Monitoring and Evaluation Directorate (MED) Capacity subcomponent will strengthen the capacity of MED to monitor the implementation of public projects and programs of NDP9. 3.2 Supporting Economic Policy Analysis and Planning Capacity subcomponent will support the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) authorities in developing economic policies, rebuilding institutions of economic management, and enhancing institutional capacity necessary for policy formulation and implementation. 4. Project Management component will provide support to the Recipient to strengthen its capacity for project planning and budgeting, management, coordination, monitoring and evaluation activities, all through the provision of technical advisory services, training, operating costs and the acquisition of goods.

recipient: Somalia (SOM); recipient organisation not named, recipient unspecified
title: Statistical support to Somalia phase II
description: Statistics Sweden has applied to Sida to initiate a second phase (2020 - 2022) of a statistical collaboration with the overall aim of strengthening the capacity of the statistical authorities in Somalia. Phase I ran between 2015 and 2019 and this second phase is now aiming at consolidating and developing the capacity and knowledge acquired by the participating Somali authorities in the first phase.This will be done by continuing to support the Somali statistical authorities. The overall objective of the project is thus to:Strengthen the statistical capacity in Somalia in order to facilitate decision-makers' awareness, understanding and confidence in statistical data.The project's expected results are:1) Improved quality in the production of social and economic statistics.2) Improved and strengthened capacity among the statistical authorities in the statistical method.3) Increased access to high quality statistics and data.4) Improved and strengthened planning and organization of the statistical authorities.This second phase is expected to strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the Statistics Office of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) and of the Statistics Office of Puntland. Somaliland has been part of phase I of this effort and the ambition is to have them included again in this second phase.

recipient: SOM; SCB/Statistiska centralbyrån, named as transaction receiver
title: Statistical support to Somalia
description: Statistics Sweden (SCB) in collaboration with Directorate of Statistics of the Federal Government of Somalia, the statistics departments of in Puntland and Somaliland has submitted a SEK 47 879 000 proposal to Sweden for funding between 2015-18. The project “Capacity Building in Statistics” aims at building the statistical capacity of the Somali Ministries of Planning and improve on availability, accuracy, and reliability of statistical data. The project will specifically provide support in the following areas; 1) Strengthening statistical systems, 2) improving the quality of economic statistics, 3) improving on the availability and quality of social statistics, and 4) improving the capacity of the national staff in statistical methodology. Sweden had earlier engaged SCB to carry out a statistical fact finding mission in order to assess possibilities and preconditions for Swedish Development cooperation with the departments of statistics in Somalia. SCB was tasked to, jointly with the Somalia statistical departments; develop a programme that will respond to the long term statistical capacity gaps of the Somali authorities. The intervention’s total budget is SEK 47 879 000, out of which Sweden will fund SEK 32 000 000. Sweden is currently the only donor to the intervention. SCB will reprioritize its activities to fit within Sweden’s allocation.
